description: Search every Notion page and data source this connection can see, by title. Returns a batch of results with the id, title, url and last edited time, plus a cursor for the next batch. Notion search matches titles only, never page body text, and only reaches pages a person has shared with the integration. Send the returned next_cursor back as `cursor` to read the next batch. Set filter_object_type to "data_source" to find the tables you can then read with notion-query_databases-1.

query.description: Text to match against page and data source titles. Omit to list everything shared with the integration.

filter_object_type.description: Return only pages, or only data sources (tables).

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous call returned.

search.description: Lenient ingress on POST /v1/search. Reads the fields the node maps and lets Notion keep adding the rest. `title` and every property value stay untyped on purpose: on a page `title` holds rich text, on a data source's property schema the same key holds the empty configuration object, and Notion's property union grows every year.

quirks.why_execute: Notion takes the cursor and the page size in the request body, not the query string, so the runtime's query-string pagination record cannot express it. A result's title also comes from one of two places: a data source carries it in a top-level rich text array, a page carries it inside whichever property has type `title`. Neither is a static mapping, so the work is code.
quirks.titles_only: Notion search matches titles, never body text. To find a phrase inside a page, search the title, then read the page with notion-read_blocks-1.
quirks.sharing: Search only reaches pages a person explicitly shared with the integration. An empty result usually means nothing was shared, not that nothing matches.
quirks.filter_value: Since API version 2025-09-03 the object filter takes "page" or "data_source"; "database" is gone.
quirks.no_fan_out: Search is the one Notion endpoint that is already batch-shaped — one request, many objects — so this node makes exactly one provider call.
